subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK requirements

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap of what we heard and agreed as next steps so everyone is aligned.

Pain points you called out:
- Long latency on your current embedding + reranking pipeline during peak traffic (~600ms 95p today).
- Inconsistent structured outputs from the product classification model, making downstream ingestion messy.
- Need for streaming responses for the live chat UI and support for function calling to trigger downstream workflows (ticket creation, metadata enrichment).

Goals / success criteria:
- Reduce reranking end-to-end latency to <300ms 95p for the search/recommendation flow.
- Deliver a structured JSON output for classification with schema enforcement (so your ETL is deterministic).
- Enable streaming for the chat UI and reliable tool invocations via function calling.

Product fit summary (how Redwood helps):
- SDK + streaming: our SDK supports token-level streaming and client-side partial parses, so your UI can render progressively.
- Function calling: Redwood supports function/tool calling semantics and structured-output constraints to safely return JSON objects that map to your ticket schema.
- Embeddings + reranking: we can host a tuned embedding + lightweight reranker variant and use prefix/KV caching + batching to hit the latency targets at predictable cost.

Technical notes we agreed to validate in the POC:
1) SDK changes: you will need to adopt the new streaming callback (see attached redwood-sdk-changes.pdf) — low-friction for JS + Python.
2) Input/output schema: we’ll work from the sample schema you provided; Redwood's structured output feature can enforce/validate the JSON shape during generation.
3) Dataset & scale: you'll provide a representative subset (~50k queries) and peak QPS estimate so we can size Dedicated capacity or a hosted config.

Next steps / owners:
- Acme: share sample dataset + current QPS numbers (Alex) — target by Mon 8/24.
- Redwood: proposed POC config (model variant + expected cost/latency) and integration checklist (Marissa) — by Tue 8/25.
- Redwood Eng: loop in Rishi for pricing sizing and Stephanie for SOC 2 / security questions (Marissa).

Attachments: redwood-sdk-changes.pdf (summary of required SDK updates), acme-integration-mvp-spec.docx (template to fill).

If that looks right, Alex—I'll kick off the POC proposal once I have the dataset and QPS.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

---

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 18:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK requirements

Thanks Marissa — solid notes, appreciate the clear next steps. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Dataset: we'll export ~50k recent queries and a small labeled set for the classifier (should have it to you by Monday EOD).
2) QPS: baseline is ~40 QPS peak for search, but bursts to 120 QPS during promotions. Latency SLOs are customer-facing so the <300ms 95p target is critical.
3) Streaming: our web team uses the React SDK; the streaming callback and incremental parse look fine. Any breaking changes to existing auth flow?

Also, on the structured output—can Redwood validate that the model never returns extra fields? That's important for our downstream ETL.

CCing Priya who owns security/compliance. We'll need Stephanie's SOC2 artifact and a short note on data residency (we're US-only).

Best,
Alex
Head of Search & Recommendations | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 07:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK requirements

Great — thanks Alex. To answer your questions:

- Auth: no breaking changes required. The SDK supports the same API key / bearer token flow you use today; streaming hooks are opt-in. We'll include small migration snippets in the SDK patch notes (attached).
- Structured outputs: yes, Redwood supports strict schema enforcement (we can reject or attempt repairs). For the POC we'll run a guarded mode that fails the request if the model deviates from the schema and surface the exact diff so your ETL can handle it deterministically.
- Data residency: Redwood hosted US regions only for this POC; we can provide a VPC/Private deployment conversation if you need on-prem or specific KMS/HSM controls.

Rishi / Stephanie — can you confirm availability to join a short sizing/pricing sync on Tue 8/25 at 10am PT? Rishi for capacity + pricing guidance, Stephanie for SOC2 artifact and notes on data retention/audit logs.

Alex / Priya — I'll push the POC proposal draft to the HubSpot record and share a Drive link once it's ready.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK requirements

Thanks for the ping — I can join Tue 8/25 10am PT. Preliminary notes from a sizing/pricing POV:
- For baseline 40 QPS, bursts to 120 QPS: recommend starting with a Dedicated small pool (2x A100-equivalent) with autoscale burst to handle promotions; we'll run the POC on a hosted config and then map to Dedicated TCO.
- Estimated POC cost (hosted): ~$3.5k–$5k for a 2-week run depending on model choices and KV cache hit rates.
- We'll include a configuration that uses a smaller reranker model (quantized) for low-latency hot-path plus a higher-quality variant for offline/regression checks.

Stephanie — can you attach the SOC 2 Type II summary and a short note on audit logs/data retention we can share with Acme?

Rishi
Head of Infrastructure Economics | Redwood Inference
